items.title: 71231_Sam Wooding Oral History Interview
items.q: but we had a Jewish fellow with us named Goldberg.

ctx.x: But tell me, where did you -- did you have to rehearse, then, before you actually went on in Berlin?

I don't know how Arthur Lyons got that show on. For the simple reason that they had -- most of the stagehands were Russian. Germans were there and the Russians and English. Now, it was more of a bedlam. It was more bedlam because the Russians -- and that's when I knew and Arthur asked me -- and he was talking Russian. And then he couldn't speak German, but we had a Jewish fellow with us named Goldberg. Goldberg spoke Yiddish. So Yiddish and German were the same, and he was talking Yiddish, Arthur Lyons was…
And none of you understood any of it.
